```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6,
                      fig.height = 3.2, fig.align = "center")
library(karma2d)
```

This vignette documents the statistical formulation implemented in `karma2d`,
following Pereira, Palm and Bayer (2026), and records where the package
deliberately differs from the article (the conditional Fisher information).
No theoretical property of the process itself (for example stationarity or
invertibility conditions on the coefficients) is claimed here: these remain
open problems, and the package does not check them.

## The Kumaraswamy distribution in the median parametrization

The Kumaraswamy distribution with shape parameters $\varphi > 0$ and
$\delta > 0$ has density
$$
f(y) = \varphi\,\delta\,y^{\varphi-1}\,(1-y^{\varphi})^{\delta-1},
\qquad 0 < y < 1 .
$$
Reparametrizing by the median $\mu \in (0,1)$ requires
$F(\mu) = 1/2$, which gives
$$
\delta = \frac{\log 0.5}{\log\left(1-\mu^{\varphi}\right)} .
$$
The distribution function and the quantile function are
$$
F(y) = 1-\left(1-y^{\varphi}\right)^{\delta},
\qquad
Q(p) = \left[1-(1-p)^{1/\delta}\right]^{1/\varphi}.
$$
These are available as `dkuma()`, `pkuma()`, `qkuma()` and `rkuma()`. For a
general support $(a, b)$ the variable is rescaled to $(y-a)/(b-a)$; the median
`median` and the arguments of the functions refer to the **original** scale.

```{r kuma}
mu <- 0.4
phi <- 5
pkuma(mu, median = mu, shape = phi)                 # 0.5 by construction
qkuma(0.5, median = mu, shape = phi)
# Support (-1, 1): median on the original scale
pkuma(0.2, median = 0.2, shape = phi, lower = -1, upper = 1)
# The density integrates to one
integrate(dkuma, 0, 1, median = mu, shape = phi)$value
```

## The 2-D KARMA model

Let $y[n,m]$ be the pixel in row $n$ and column $m$, conditionally
Kumaraswamy with median $\mu[n,m]$ and shape $\varphi$, given the pixels in
its strongly causal neighbourhood. With a strictly increasing differentiable
link $g:(0,1)\to\mathbb{R}$ (logit by default; probit, cloglog and cauchit are
also available), the linear predictor is
$$
\eta[n,m] = g(\mu[n,m]) = \alpha
 + \sum_{(i,j)} \phi_{(i,j)}\, g\!\left(y[n-i,m-j]\right)
 + \sum_{(k,l)} \theta_{(k,l)}\, e[n-k,m-l],
$$
with errors $e[n,m] = g(y[n,m]) - \eta[n,m]$. The AR sum runs over
$i,j \in \{0,\dots,p\}$ and the MA sum over $k,l \in \{0,\dots,q\}$,
excluding $(0,0)$.

**Lag convention.** In $\phi_{(i,j)}$ the first index $i$ is the **row** lag
and the second index $j$ the **column** lag. The coefficients are stored in the
order $(0,1),(0,2),\dots,(0,p),(1,0),(1,1),\dots,(p,p)$ (row lag varying
slowest), so that an order-$p$ model has $(p+1)^2-1$ coefficients:

```{r lags}
karma2d_lags(1)
karma2d_lags(2)
```

## Conditional likelihood

Pixels with $n \le w$ or $m \le w$, where $w = \max(p, q)$, do not have a
complete neighbourhood. The likelihood is conditional on them: the recursion
starts with $e = 0$ on these borders, and only the pixels with row and column
greater than $w$ contribute,
$$
\ell(\gamma,\varphi) = \sum_{n=w+1}^{N}\sum_{m=w+1}^{M}
 \Big[\log\varphi + \log\delta[n,m] + (\varphi-1)\log y[n,m]
 + (\delta[n,m]-1)\log\left(1-y[n,m]^{\varphi}\right)\Big],
$$
where $\gamma = (\alpha, \phi^\top, \theta^\top)^\top$ and $\delta[n,m]$ is
computed from $\mu[n,m] = g^{-1}(\eta[n,m])$. The number of pixels used is
$(N-w)(M-w)$, returned by `nobs()`.

## Optimization

`karma2d_fit()` maximizes $\ell$ with `stats::optim(method = "BFGS")` and the
analytic score (below). The shape is optimized on the log scale,
$\vartheta = \log\varphi$, so every trial value is valid; the score is
transformed by the chain rule,
$\partial\ell/\partial\vartheta = \varphi\,\partial\ell/\partial\varphi$, and
estimates are reported for $\varphi$. This can be changed with
`karma2d_control(shape_transform = "identity")`.

Starting values (see `karma2d_start()`) are $\alpha_0 = g(\bar y)$, all AR and
MA coefficients equal to zero, and
$\varphi_0 = 0.3\,\big(\bar y(1-\bar y)/S^2 - 1\big)$, with $\bar y$ and $S^2$
the sample mean and variance of the rescaled image. If this value is not
positive, the shape starts at 1 with a warning.

```{r start}
y <- karma2d_simulate(20, 20, alpha = 0.2, ar = c(0.3, 0.2, -0.1),
                      shape = 8, seed = 3)
karma2d_start(y, order = c(1, 0))
```

## Score vector

Write $u = \mu^{\varphi}$, $L = \log(1-u)$, so that $\delta = \log(0.5)/L$, and
$$
A = \frac{\varphi\,\mu^{\varphi-1}}{(1-u)\,L},
\qquad
B = \frac{u\log\mu}{(1-u)\,L}
\quad\Big(= \tfrac{1}{\delta}\,\tfrac{\partial\delta}{\partial\varphi}\Big).
$$
Per pixel,
$$
\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = A\,\big[1+\delta\log(1-y^{\varphi})\big],
\qquad
\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \varphi} = \frac1\varphi + \log y
 + B\,\big[1+\delta\log(1-y^{\varphi})\big]
 - (\delta-1)\frac{y^{\varphi}\log y}{1-y^{\varphi}} .
$$
By the chain rule, for $\gamma_k$ a component of $\gamma$,
$$
\frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\gamma_k} = \sum_{n,m}
 \frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\mu[n,m]}\,
 \frac{d\mu[n,m]}{d\eta[n,m]}\,
 \frac{\partial\eta[n,m]}{\partial\gamma_k}.
$$
The derivatives of the linear predictor satisfy recursions over the same
neighbourhood (Appendix A of the article), with zeros on the borders:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial\eta[n,m]}{\partial\alpha} &= 1 - \sum_{(s,t)}\theta_{(s,t)}
  \frac{\partial\eta[n-s,m-t]}{\partial\alpha},\\
\frac{\partial\eta[n,m]}{\partial\phi_{(i,j)}} &= g(y[n-i,m-j]) - \sum_{(s,t)}\theta_{(s,t)}
  \frac{\partial\eta[n-s,m-t]}{\partial\phi_{(i,j)}},\\
\frac{\partial\eta[n,m]}{\partial\theta_{(k,l)}} &= e[n-k,m-l] - \sum_{(s,t)}\theta_{(s,t)}
  \frac{\partial\eta[n-s,m-t]}{\partial\theta_{(k,l)}}.
\end{aligned}
$$
`karma2d_score()` evaluates this score; a quick check against central
differences of `karma2d_loglik()`:

```{r score}
par_true <- c(alpha = 0.2, 0.3, 0.2, -0.1, shape = 8)
s_analytic <- karma2d_score(y, par_true, order = c(1, 0))
s_numeric <- vapply(seq_along(par_true), function(k) {
  h <- 1e-5
  up <- par_true
  dn <- par_true
  up[k] <- up[k] + h
  dn[k] <- dn[k] - h
  (karma2d_loglik(y, up, c(1, 0)) - karma2d_loglik(y, dn, c(1, 0))) / (2 * h)
}, numeric(1))
cbind(analytic = s_analytic, numeric = s_numeric)
```

## Conditional Fisher information (corrected)

The package computes the conditional expected information in closed form per
pixel. Two facts about the model drive the calculation. If $Y$ is Kumaraswamy
with median $\mu$ and shape $\varphi$, then

* $E = -\delta\log(1-Y^{\varphi}) \sim \text{Exp}(1)$, and
* $X = Y^{\varphi} \sim \text{Beta}(1,\delta)$,

and the $\mu$-score is $\partial\ell/\partial\mu = A\,(1-E)$. Define
$$
h(\delta) = \frac{\psi(2)-\psi(\delta+1)}{\delta-1},
\qquad
t(\delta) = \frac{\big(\psi(\delta)-\psi(2)\big)^2+\psi'(2)-\psi'(\delta)}{\delta-2},
$$
with $\psi$ the digamma function. Both have removable singularities
(at $\delta=1$ and $\delta=2$) which the package handles. The per-pixel
expected information is
$$
\begin{aligned}
K_{\mu\mu} &= A^2,\\
K_{\mu\varphi} &= A\Big(B + \frac{\delta\,h(\delta)}{\varphi}\Big),\\
K_{\varphi\varphi} &= \frac{1}{\varphi^2} + B^2
 + \frac{2\delta B\,h(\delta)}{\varphi} + \frac{\delta\,t(\delta)}{\varphi^2}.
\end{aligned}
$$
For the whole image, with $D[n,m] = \partial\eta[n,m]/\partial\gamma$ and sums
over the effective region,
$$
K_{\gamma\gamma} = \sum K_{\mu\mu}\Big(\frac{d\mu}{d\eta}\Big)^2 D D^\top,
\qquad
K_{\gamma\varphi} = \sum K_{\mu\varphi}\,\frac{d\mu}{d\eta}\,D,
\qquad
K_{\varphi\varphi}\ \text{summed over pixels.}
$$

### Differences with Appendix B of the article

In the notation of the article, with
$\lambda_k = \mu^{k\varphi-2}/\big((1-u)^k L^k\big)$ and
$\kappa$ the Euler constant, the corrected quantities are
$$
K_{\varphi\varphi} = \frac1{\varphi^2} + \mu^2\lambda_2\log^2\mu
 + 2\delta\mu^2\log\mu\,\lambda_1\,\frac{1-\psi(\delta+1)-\kappa}{(\delta-1)\varphi}
 + \delta\,\frac{\psi(\delta)\big(\psi(\delta)+2(\kappa-1)\big)-\psi'(\delta)+k_0}
 {(\delta-2)\varphi^2},
$$
where $k_0$ is the constant defined in the article (it collects the
$\psi(2)$ and $\psi'(2)$ terms), and the last two terms together equal
$2\delta B\,h(\delta)/\varphi + \delta\,t(\delta)/\varphi^2$ in the notation above.
Appendix B of the article has **minus** signs on the second
and fourth terms. With those signs $K_{\varphi\varphi}$ can be negative: for
$\mu = 0.5$ and $\varphi = 3$ it gives $-1.55$, whereas the correct value is
$0.161$. Likewise $K_{\mu\varphi}$ above equals minus the article's
$d[n,m]$. The sign of $K_{\gamma\varphi}$ does not affect the standard
errors (it is equivalent to $\varphi \mapsto -\varphi$), but the errors in
$K_{\varphi\varphi}$ do. The formulas used by the package were verified
against numerical integration to about eight significant digits for $\delta$
from $0.25$ to $2400$, and the package test suite repeats this check.

### A pixel-level numerical check

Using $E\sim\text{Exp}(1)$, put $t = E \in (0,\infty)$; then
$y^{\varphi} = 1-\exp(-t/\delta)$, and the score for $\varphi$ is an explicit
function of $t$. Its expected square, $\int s(t)^2 e^{-t}\,dt$, must equal
$K_{\varphi\varphi}$.

```{r pixel-check}
mu <- 0.5
phi <- 3
u <- mu^phi
log1mu <- log1p(-u)
delta <- log(0.5) / log1mu
b_term <- u * log(mu) / ((1 - u) * log1mu)
h <- (digamma(2) - digamma(delta + 1)) / (delta - 1)
tt <- ((digamma(delta) - digamma(2))^2 + trigamma(2) - trigamma(delta)) /
  (delta - 2)
k_phiphi <- 1 / phi^2 + b_term^2 + 2 * delta * b_term * h / phi +
  delta * tt / phi^2

# Score for phi as a function of t = -delta * log(1 - y^phi)
score_phi <- function(t) {
  log_y <- log(-expm1(-t / delta)) / phi
  # ratio of y^phi to one minus y^phi
  ratio <- expm1(t / delta)
  1 / phi + log_y + b_term * (1 - t) - (delta - 1) * ratio * log_y
}
k_numeric <- integrate(function(t) score_phi(t)^2 * exp(-t), 0, 60)$value
c(closed_form = k_phiphi, integrate = k_numeric)
```

### Expected versus observed information on an image

`karma2d_information()` returns the expected information at given parameter
values; `type = "observed"` returns minus the Hessian of the log-likelihood
(central differences of the analytic score). They are close, not identical, on
a finite image:

```{r information}
fit <- karma2d_fit(y, order = c(1, 0))
info_exp <- karma2d_information(y, coef(fit), order = c(1, 0))
info_obs <- karma2d_information(y, coef(fit), order = c(1, 0),
                                type = "observed")
round(info_exp, 1)
round(info_obs, 1)
# Standard errors implied by each
rbind(expected = sqrt(diag(solve(info_exp))),
      observed = sqrt(diag(solve(info_obs))))
# karma2d_fisher() does the same starting from a fitted object
all.equal(karma2d_fisher(fit), info_exp)
```

## Residuals

The residuals of a fit are the quantile residuals
$$
r[n,m] = \Phi^{-1}\!\Big(F\big(y[n,m]\mid\hat\mu[n,m],\hat\varphi\big)\Big),
$$
with $\Phi$ the standard normal distribution function. They are computed from
whichever tail of $F$ is smaller to avoid overflow for extreme pixels. They
are `NA` on the borders unless padding is used (next section).
`karma2d_residuals()` also supports `type = "response"` and `type = "link"`,
and residuals for new images.

```{r residuals}
r <- residuals(fit)
c(mean = mean(r, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(r, na.rm = TRUE))
```

## Prediction at the borders

Without padding, `predict()` returns `NA` for the first $w$ rows and columns.
With `padding = "duplicate"` the image is extended before filtering: the
first $2w$ rows are copied on top of the image, then the first $2w$ columns of
the result are copied on its left, giving an $(N+2w)\times(M+2w)$ array; the
filter is run on it and the original window is returned. The article calls
this "mirror padding", but the rows and columns are copied **without being
reversed**, exactly as in the original scripts, and the package follows that
behaviour.

```{r padding}
pred <- predict(fit, padding = "duplicate")
sum(is.na(pred))
# For an autoregressive model (q = 0) the interior pixels do not depend on
# the padding, so they coincide with the unpadded predictions
p0 <- predict(fit)
all.equal(pred[-1, -1], p0[-1, -1])
```

## Reference

Pereira, V. B. S., Palm, B. G. and Bayer, F. M. (2026). A Kumaraswamy-based
spatial model for bounded image data. Manuscript.
